key_insight: In this rheumatology study—not cancer drug discovery—physician-reviewed, LLM-generated discharge letters improved readability and assessed understandability compared with standard letters.
clinical_relevance: Patient-friendly letters may support communication after a new rheumatic or musculoskeletal diagnosis, but improved patient comprehension and clinical outcomes remain unproven.
method: Prospective, single-centre, single-arm feasibility study enrolling 58 patients.
GPT models simplified standard discharge letters; physicians reviewed drafts before patients received both versions.
Evaluated review time, medical discrepancies, information fidelity, readability and patient feedback.
evidence_signal: Readability increased by 11.4 Flesch points and assessed understandability by 10.0 percentage points; 44/51 follow-up respondents (86.3%) wanted similar letters in future.
watch_item: Unedited drafts contained 11 medical discrepancies across 10/58 letters; ten discrepancies were corrected before discharge, underscoring the need for physician oversight.
paper_title: LLM-generated patient-friendly discharge letters for newly diagnosed rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases: a prospective feasibility study
